meta.title: Marathon coach professional asset registry
meta.scope: Primary and high-level secondary sources that constrain marathon plan generation, adaptation, race pacing, fuelling, hydration, recovery, safety, and calendar export.
meta.evidence_policy: Prefer governing-body consensus, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and peer-reviewed primary studies. Observational associations and practice audits may guide conservative defaults but must not be presented as causal rules.

governing_body_and_consensus.title: International Association of Athletics Federations Consensus Statement 2019: Nutrition for Athletics
decision_use: Periodize and individualize nutrition to training and competition demands.
Escalate persistent low-energy-availability concerns to qualified sports nutrition and medical professionals.
limitations: Consensus principles require individual translation; they are not a fixed meal plan.

governing_body_and_consensus.title: Contemporary Nutrition Strategies to Optimize Performance in Distance Runners and Race Walkers
decision_use: Rehearse race carbohydrate and fluid strategies during long runs.
For the longest races, high carbohydrate delivery may reach 75-90 g/hour when practiced and tolerated.
limitations: The upper intake range is not an automatic starting target and may cause gastrointestinal distress without progressive gut training.

governing_body_and_consensus.title: 2023 International Olympic Committee consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport
decision_use: Do not pair escalating marathon load with chronic under-fuelling or aggressive weight loss.
Flag persistent fatigue, recurrent bone injury, menstrual disruption, low libido, or deteriorating performance for professional review.
limitations: REDs is a clinical, multifactorial diagnosis; the skill can screen for concerns but cannot diagnose it.

governing_body_and_consensus.title: Updating ACSM's Recommendations for Exercise Preparticipation Health Screening
decision_use: Screen current activity, known cardiovascular/metabolic/renal disease, warning symptoms, and desired intensity before hard training.
limitations: Screening determines whether medical clearance is prudent; it does not establish marathon readiness.

governing_body_and_consensus.title: Statement of the Third International Exercise-Associated Hyponatremia Consensus Development Conference
decision_use: Warn against fluid intake in excess of losses and use thirst as the default safety guide.
Treat sodium as individualized support, not protection against overdrinking.
limitations: Environmental conditions, sweat rate, body size, medications, and race duration change individual needs.

governing_body_and_consensus.title: Sleep and the athlete: narrative review and 2021 expert consensus recommendations
decision_use: Use individualized sleep need and recent sleep disruption as readiness context rather than one universal target.
Reduce training stress when sleep inadequacy coexists with other fatigue or illness signals.
limitations: The paper notes that much athlete sleep evidence is low quality and a universal 7-9 hour rule is not ideal.

governing_body_and_consensus.title: Recovery and Performance in Sport: Consensus Statement
decision_use: Monitor recovery with multiple subjective and objective signals and adjust training for individual response.
limitations: No single readiness metric reliably captures recovery or injury risk.

systematic_reviews_and_meta_analyses.title: Which Training Intensity Distribution Intervention Will Produce the Greatest Improvements in Endurance Athletes?
systematic_reviews_and_meta_analyses.evidence_type: systematic review and individual-participant network meta-analysis
decision_use: Keep most training low intensity and a smaller portion moderate/high, while adapting pyramidal versus polarized emphasis to level and response.
Do not claim one universal intensity distribution is superior for every runner.
limitations: Only 13 studies and 348 athletes were included; women were underrepresented and outcomes were VO2max/time trial rather than marathon performance.

systematic_reviews_and_meta_analyses.title: Effect of Strength Training Programs in Middle- and Long-Distance Runners' Economy at Different Running Speeds
decision_use: Include progressive heavy, plyometric, or combined strength work when technically appropriate.
Reduce strength fatigue near key marathon-specific sessions and during taper.
limitations: Evidence certainty ranged from moderate to low; included programs and runner levels were heterogeneous.

systematic_reviews_and_meta_analyses.title: Effects of Tapering on Performance: A Meta-Analysis
decision_use: Use a roughly two-week default taper with a substantial volume reduction while retaining short intensity and normal training rhythm where tolerated.
limitations: The analysis spans multiple sports and competitive athletes; individual marathon response and longer tapers can differ.

systematic_reviews_and_meta_analyses.title: An Evaluation of the Training Determinants of Marathon Performance
decision_use: Treat sustained weekly volume, run frequency, long-run preparation, and training history as performance-relevant inputs.
limitations: Associations across heterogeneous cohorts do not prove that simply increasing every training parameter will improve an individual runner.

systematic_reviews_and_meta_analyses.title: The Association Between Running Injuries and Training Parameters: A Systematic Review
decision_use: Avoid presenting weekly distance, duration, frequency, intensity, or a single progression percentage as a proven injury-prevention rule.
Use multi-factor monitoring that includes pain, recovery, lifestyle, and training history.
limitations: The review found conflicting evidence and wide variation in injury definitions and study designs.

systematic_reviews_and_meta_analyses.title: Pacing Strategies in Marathons: A Systematic Review
decision_use: Build race plans around controlled, low-variability pacing and adapt for performance level, course, environment, age, and sex.
Do not treat the positive splits commonly observed in results as the desired strategy.
limitations: Most included studies were observational and optimal pacing depends on course and athlete context.

primary_and_practice_evidence.title: How Much Running Is Too Much? Identifying High-Risk Running Sessions in a 5200-Person Cohort Study
decision_use: Flag a planned single run that exceeds the longest run in the prior 30 days by more than 10%.
Do not substitute weekly acute:chronic ratios for the single-session check.
limitations: Observational association based on self-reported overuse injury; it does not prove a universal causal threshold or cover every runner.

primary_and_practice_evidence.title: Quantitative Analysis of 92 12-Week Sub-Elite Marathon Training Plans
decision_use: Use low/middle/high plan-volume bands as practice context, never as a required target.
Prefer a pyramidal default for recreational runners unless their history supports a different distribution.
limitations: The authors explicitly note that the audit does not demonstrate the effectiveness of the plans reviewed.

primary_and_practice_evidence.title: Pacing Strategy Patterns and Performance Outcomes in Marathon Running
decision_use: Use even effort/low pace variability as the default target and avoid an aggressive first half.
Explain that course topography and weather may require pace variation to preserve even effort.
limitations: Boston Marathon data are observational and course-specific; association with faster times does not establish causation.

primary_and_practice_evidence.title: Marathon Pacing Ability: Training Characteristics and Previous Experience
decision_use: Use prior races, recent personal bests, and accumulated volume to qualify confidence in a goal pace.
limitations: Small questionnaire-based cohort and correlational design.

primary_and_practice_evidence.title: Athletic Records and Human Endurance
decision_use: Use the Riegel time-distance relationship only as a labelled planning estimate from a recent race result.
limitations: Population-level modelling cannot account for marathon-specific durability, course, weather, fuelling, or individual physiology.

technical_standards.title: RFC 5545: Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification
decision_use: Generate interoperable VEVENT records with escaped text, stable UIDs, DTSTART, DTEND, SUMMARY, and DESCRIPTION.
limitations: Calendar applications differ in timezone and import behavior; live installation remains platform-specific.
